name: Nebat
overview: Nebat was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as the father of Jeroboam. He was an Ephraimite from the town of Zeredah, as recorded in 1 Kings 11:26. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about Nebat.
namesAndTitles: The name Nebat means 'look to, regard [approvingly],' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a positive connotation. This name was not given directly by God but is noted in the biblical text in 1 Kings 11:26.
familyAndRelationships: Nebat is identified explicitly as the father of Jeroboam, a significant biblical figure. He is also described as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim. Scripture does not record additional family relationships beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Nebat's significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as the father of Jeroboam, who became a prominent leader in Israel. His identification as an Ephraimite situates him within the northern kingdom's tribal context, providing background to Jeroboam's heritage. Although Nebat himself does not play a direct role in the events recorded, his lineage is important for understanding the origins of Jeroboam's leadership.
